```{r}
plotting_data <- brca1_df %>%
  drop_na(function_score, ESM.1v)

# 1. Load PDB (Ensure this path is correct)
pdb_path <- "~/Downloads/AF-P38398-F1-model_v6.pdb"
pdb <- read.pdb(pdb_path)

# 2. Define Active Sites
active_site_resnos <- c(
    24,27,39,41,44,47,61,64,           # RING
    3,6,7,8,10,11,14,15,17,18,21,22,38,76,77,78,79,81,82,85,88,89,92,93,96,97,
    1654, 1655, 1656, 1657, 1658, 1690, 1691, 1696, # BRCT
    1698,1699,1700,1701,1702,1740,1741,1773,
    1774,1775,1811,1813,1836,1839
)

# 3. Get Active Site Coordinates (Using the CORRECT 'string' argument)
# This was likely the missing piece in your previous environment
site_inds <- atom.select(pdb, resno = active_site_resnos, string = "noh")
site_xyz <- pdb$xyz[site_inds$xyz]

# Check immediately
if (length(site_inds$atom) == 0) {
  stop("STOP: Active site atoms are 0. The Code will not work.")
} else {
  print(paste("Active Site Loaded: Found", length(site_inds$atom), "atoms."))
}

# 4. Redefine the Function (The Robust Version)
calc_min_heavy_dist <- function(res_num, pdb_obj, site_coords) {
  
  # Bio3D is strict: 'resno' must be numeric. 
  # We force it here to fix the error you saw in Test B.
  res_num <- as.numeric(as.character(res_num))
  
  # Use 'string = "noh"' (The fix confirmed by Test A)
  target_inds <- atom.select(pdb_obj, resno = res_num, string = "noh")
  
  # Safety catch for missing residues
  if (length(target_inds$atom) == 0) return(NA)
  
  # Calculate
  target_xyz <- pdb_obj$xyz[target_inds$xyz]
  t_mat <- matrix(target_xyz, ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)
  s_mat <- matrix(site_coords, ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)
  
  return(min(dist.xyz(t_mat, s_mat), na.rm = TRUE))
}

# 5. Run Calculation
unique_positions <- unique(plotting_data$mutation_position)

print("Starting calculation loop...")

dist_vals <- sapply(unique_positions, function(x) {
  calc_min_heavy_dist(x, pdb, site_xyz)
})

# 6. Map Back Safely
# explicitly name the vector to ensure matching works
names(dist_vals) <- as.character(unique_positions) 

# Assign based on character matching
plotting_data$min_dist_to_site <- dist_vals[as.character(plotting_data$mutation_position)]

# 7. Final Result
print(paste("Final NAs:", sum(is.na(plotting_data$min_dist_to_site))))
head(plotting_data$min_dist_to_site)

# If NAs remain, it means those specific residues are missing from the PDB structure 
# (common in loop regions), which is normal.
# Filter out NAs (residues not found in PDB structure)
plotting_data <- plotting_data %>% filter(!is.na(min_dist_to_site))
nrow(plotting_data) #1837

# --- ANALYSIS 1: VARIANCE PARTITIONING (THE "DELTA") ---
# Model A: Stability Alone
mod_stab <- lm(function_score ~ ddG_pred, data = plotting_data)
r2_stab <- summary(mod_stab)$r.squared

# Model B: Stability + ESM1v
mod_full <- lm(function_score ~ ddG_pred + ESM.1v, data = plotting_data)
r2_full <- summary(mod_full)$r.squared

r2_delta <- r2_full - r2_stab

# PRINT THESE NUMBERS FOR YOUR TEXT
print(paste("Variance explained by Stability (R2):", round(r2_stab * 100, 1), "%"))
print(paste("Variance explained by Stability + ESM (R2):", round(r2_full * 100, 1), "%"))
print(paste("The Delta (Biological Signal):", round(r2_delta * 100, 1), "%"))

# > print(paste("Variance explained by Stability (R2):", round(r2_stab * 100, 1), "%"))
# [1] "Variance explained by Stability (R2): 22.3 %"
# > print(paste("Variance explained by Stability + ESM (R2):", round(r2_full * 100, 1), "%"))
# [1] "Variance explained by Stability + ESM (R2): 35.1 %"
# > print(paste("The Delta (Biological Signal):", round(r2_delta * 100, 1), "%"))
# [1] "The Delta (Biological Signal): 12.8 %"

# --- ANALYSIS 2: OVER-PREDICTION CHECK (SPECIFICITY) ---
# Define Thresholds (Adjust these based on standard cutoffs for SGE/ESM)
# Common SGE pathogenic cutoff is approx -1.5 to -2.0
# Common ESM1v pathogenic cutoff is approx -7.0 or bottom 10%
sge_cutoff <- -1.5 
esm_cutoff <- quantile(plotting_data$ESM.1v, 0.15) # Example: Bottom 15% are pathogenic

# Isolate "Stable" variants
stable_subset <- plotting_data %>% 
  filter(ddG_pred < 1) # Commonly accepted stability threshold 

# Create Confusion Matrix
stable_subset <- stable_subset %>%
  mutate(
    Truth = ifelse(function_score < sge_cutoff, "Pathogenic", "Benign"),
    Pred  = ifelse(ESM.1v < esm_cutoff, "Pathogenic", "Benign")
  )

confusion <- table(Predicted = stable_subset$Pred, Actual = stable_subset$Truth)
print(confusion)

# Calculate Stats
TP <- confusion["Pathogenic", "Pathogenic"]
FP <- confusion["Pathogenic", "Benign"]
TN <- confusion["Benign", "Benign"]
FN <- confusion["Benign", "Pathogenic"]

sensitivity <- TP / (TP + FN)
fpr <- FP / (FP + TN) # False Positive Rate (Over-prediction)

# PRINT THESE NUMBERS FOR YOUR TEXT
print(paste("Capture Rate (Sensitivity) on Stable Variants:", round(sensitivity * 100, 1), "%"))
print(paste("False Positive Rate (Over-prediction) on Stable Variants:", round(fpr * 100, 1), "%"))
```

```{r}
transform_score <- function(x, invert_scale = FALSE) {
  ranks <- rank(x, ties.method = "average")
  min_r <- min(ranks, na.rm = TRUE); max_r <- max(ranks, na.rm = TRUE)
  norm <- if(max_r == min_r) rep(0, length(ranks)) else (ranks - min_r) / (max_r - min_r)
  if(invert_scale) return(1 - norm) else return(norm)
}
```

```{r}
# Calculate the Two Residuals (Kept from your original code) ---
# Signal: What part of ESM1v is NOT Stability?
model_signal <- loess(ESM.1v ~ ddG_pred, data = plotting_data, span = 0.7, family = "symmetric")
plotting_data$Signal_Residual <- residuals(model_signal)

# Error: What part of SGE is NOT ESM1v?
model_error <- loess(function_score ~ ESM.1v, data = plotting_data, span = 0.7, family = "symmetric")
plotting_data$Error_Residual <- residuals(model_error)

# Exp residual: What part of SGE is NOT stability?
model_exp <- loess(function_score ~ ddG_pred, data = plotting_data, span = 0.7, family = "symmetric")
plotting_data$Exp_Residual <- residuals(model_exp)

    # Delta: Positive = SGE is higher (Under-predicted/MAVE-damaging)

    Error_norm = SGE_Pathogenicity - ESM_Pathogenicity,
    Signal_Residual_norm = transform_score(Signal_Residual, invert_scale = TRUE),
```

```{r, fig.width=12, fig.height=4.5}
# --- Calculate Statistics for the Text ---
# Correlation
spearman_val <- cor(plotting_data$Signal_Residual, plotting_data$Exp_Residual, 
                    method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs")

# Linear Model P-value (To support "significant positive slope")
lm_model <- lm(Exp_Residual ~ Signal_Residual, data = plotting_data)
lm_summary <- summary(lm_model)
p_value <- lm_summary$coefficients[2, 4] # Extract slope P-value

# Format the subtitle text dynamically
# If P is very small, use scientific notation
p_label <- ifelse(p_value < 2.2e-16, "P < 2.2e-16", sprintf("P = %.2e", p_value))
stats_subtitle <- sprintf("Spearman rho: %.3f | Slope %s", spearman_val, p_label)

# --- 3. Plot P1: Raw Comparison ---
p1 <- ggplot(plotting_data, aes(x = ESM.1v, y = function_score)) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = clinvar_group, color = clinvar_group, alpha = clinvar_group), size = 2.5) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("Pathogenic" = 17, "Benign" = 16, "Other" = 16)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Other" = "grey70", "Benign" = "#1B9E77", "Pathogenic" = "#D95F02")) +
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c("Other" = 0.5, "Benign" = 0.9, "Pathogenic" = 0.9), guide = "none") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "black", size = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "BRCA1 - Raw Scores",
    subtitle = sprintf("Spearman's rho = %.3f", 
                       cor(plotting_data$ESM.1v, plotting_data$function_score, method="spearman", use="complete.obs")),
    x = "Predicted Pathogenicity (ESM1v)",
    y = "Experimental Function (SGE)"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  ) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") 

# --- 4. Plot P2: Residual Comparison (The Main Argument) ---
p2 <- ggplot(plotting_data, aes(x = Signal_Residual, y = Exp_Residual)) +
  # Add Quadrant Lines to highlight the "Allosteric Concordance" (Bottom-Left)
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  
  # Points
  geom_point(aes(shape = clinvar_group, color = clinvar_group, alpha = clinvar_group), size = 2.5) +
  
  # Linear Regression Line (The "Significant Positive Slope")
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "black", size = 1) +
  
  # Scales
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("Pathogenic" = 17, "Benign" = 16, "Other" = 16)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Other" = "grey70", "Benign" = "#1B9E77", "Pathogenic" = "#D95F02")) +
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c("Other" = 0.5, "Benign" = 0.9, "Pathogenic" = 0.9), guide = "none") +
  
  # Labels
  labs(
    title = "Stability-independent Effects",
    subtitle = stats_subtitle, # Uses the calculated P-value < 2.2e-16
    x = "ESM1v - TMPNN Stability",
    y = "SGE - TMPNN Stability",
    shape = "ClinVar", color = "ClinVar"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

p3 <- ggplot(plotting_data, aes(x = ddG_pred, y = function_score)) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = clinvar_group, color = clinvar_group, alpha = clinvar_group), size = 2.5) +
```

```{r, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
# 4. Redefine the Function (The Robust Version)
calc_min_heavy_dist <- function(res_num, pdb_obj, site_coords) {
  
  # Bio3D is strict: 'resno' must be numeric. 
  # We force it here to fix the error you saw in Test B.
  res_num <- as.numeric(as.character(res_num))
  
  # Use 'string = "noh"' (The fix confirmed by Test A)
  target_inds <- atom.select(pdb_obj, resno = res_num, string = "noh")

  if (length(target_inds$atom) == 0) return(NA)

  t_mat <- matrix(target_xyz, ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)
  s_mat <- matrix(site_coords, ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)
  
  return(min(dist.xyz(t_mat, s_mat), na.rm = TRUE))
}

# 5. Run Calculation

# 1. Prepare Data
plot_ready <- plotting_data %>%
  dplyr::select(min_dist_to_site, Signal_Residual_norm, Error_norm, Exp_Residual_norm) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c("Exp_Residual_norm", "Signal_Residual_norm", "Error_norm"), 
               names_to = "Residual_Type", values_to = "Value") %>%
  mutate(Abs_Value = abs(Value)) %>%
  # Bin data into 5 Angstrom chunks
  mutate(Dist_Bin = cut(min_dist_to_site, breaks = seq(0, 60, by = 5), include.lowest = TRUE)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Dist_Bin)) %>% 
  group_by(Dist_Bin, Residual_Type) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean_Resid = mean(Abs_Value),
    SE = sd(Abs_Value) / sqrt(n()), 
    Distance_Center = as.numeric(sub("\\((.+),.*", "\\1", Dist_Bin)) + 2.5
  )

# 2. Define Colors and Labels
# We define them explicitly here to ensure they match
my_colors <- c("Exp_Residual_norm" = "darkblue","Signal_Residual_norm" = "#D55E00", "Error_norm" = "grey40")

# 3. Plot with Fixed Legend Order
p_binned <- ggplot(plot_ready, aes(x = Distance_Center, y = Mean_Resid, color = Residual_Type)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = Mean_Resid - SE, ymax = Mean_Resid + SE), width = 1.5) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +  # Note: use 'size' if you have older ggplot2
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  
  # --- THE FIX IS HERE ---
  scale_color_manual(
    values = my_colors,
    # 'breaks' determines the ORDER in the legend
    breaks = c("Exp_Residual_norm","Signal_Residual_norm", "Error_norm"), 
    # 'labels' determines the TEXT shown
    labels = c("SGE-ddGf residual (Signal)","ESM-1v-ddGf residual (Pred)", "SGE-ESM-1v delta (Error)")
  ) +
  # -----------------------

  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(title = "Spatial Decay of ESM1v Signal vs. Error",
       subtitle = "BRCA1",
       x = "Minimum Heavy Atom Distance to Active/Binding Site (Å)",
       y = "Mean Residual Magnitude",
       color = NULL) + # NULL removes the legend title "Residual_Type"
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.background = element_rect(fill=alpha('white', 0.8), color="black", size=0.2))

print(p_binned)
```

```{r, fig.width=6, fig.height=4}
    1654, 1655, 1656, 1657, 1658, 1690, 1691, 1696,
    1698,1699,1700,1701,1702,1740,1741,1773,
    1774,1775,1811,1813,1836,1839 # BRCT
)

# 3. Get Active Site Coordinates (Using the CORRECT 'string' argument)
# This was likely the missing piece in your previous environment
site_inds <- atom.select(pdb, resno = active_site_resnos, string = "noh")
site_xyz <- pdb$xyz[site_inds$xyz]

# Check immediately
if (length(site_inds$atom) == 0) {
  stop("STOP: Active site atoms are 0. The Code will not work.")
} else {
  print(paste("Active Site Loaded: Found", length(site_inds$atom), "atoms."))
}

# 4. Redefine the Function (The Robust Version)
calc_min_heavy_dist <- function(res_num, pdb_obj, site_coords) {
  
  # Bio3D is strict: 'resno' must be numeric. 
  # We force it here to fix the error you saw in Test B.
  res_num <- as.numeric(as.character(res_num))
  
  # Use 'string = "noh"' (The fix confirmed by Test A)
  target_inds <- atom.select(pdb_obj, resno = res_num, string = "noh")
  
  # Safety catch for missing residues
  if (length(target_inds$atom) == 0) return(NA)
  
  # Calculate
  target_xyz <- pdb_obj$xyz[target_inds$xyz]
  t_mat <- matrix(target_xyz, ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)
  s_mat <- matrix(site_coords, ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)
  
  return(min(dist.xyz(t_mat, s_mat), na.rm = TRUE))
}
```

```{r}
# --- Analysis 1: Variance Partitioning (Quantifying "How Much") ---
# Model A: Stability Alone (How well does stability explain function?)
model_stab <- lm(function_score ~ ddG_pred, data = plotting_data)
r2_stab <- summary(model_stab)$r.squared

# Model B: Stability + ESM1v (How much does adding ESM1v improve it?)
model_combined <- lm(function_score ~ ddG_pred + ESM.1v, data = plotting_data)
r2_combined <- summary(model_combined)$r.squared

# The "Delta" (Unique contribution of ESM1v/Allostery)
r2_delta <- r2_combined - r2_stab

print(paste("R2 Stability:", round(r2_stab, 3)))
print(paste("R2 Combined:", round(r2_combined, 3)))
print(paste("Added Value (The Signal):", round(r2_delta, 3)))
print(paste("Unexplained (The 'Missing' Function):", round(1 - r2_combined, 3)))

# --- Analysis 2: The "Allosteric Confusion Matrix" (Addressing Over-prediction) ---
# 1. Isolate STABLE variants (e.g., ddG < 1 or similar threshold)
# Note: Adjust thresholds based on your previous definitions
stable_subset <- plotting_data %>% 
  filter(ddG_pred < 1) %>%  # "Stable"
  mutate(
    # Ground Truth: Is it ACTUALLY pathogenic? (SGE < threshold)
    # Adjust -1.5 to  SGE pathogenic cutoff
    is_pathogenic_exp = ifelse(function_score < -1.5, "Pathogenic", "Benign"),
    
    # Prediction: Does ESM1v SAY it's pathogenic? (ESM1v < threshold)
    # Adjust -7 to  ESM1v pathogenic cutoff
    is_pathogenic_pred = ifelse(ESM.1v < -7, "Pathogenic", "Benign")
  )

# 2. Confusion Matrix for Stable Variants
confusion <- table(Predicted = stable_subset$is_pathogenic_pred, 
                   Actual = stable_subset$is_pathogenic_exp)
print(confusion)

# 3. Calculate Rates
# False Positive Rate (Over-prediction): Pred Path / Actual Benign
fpr <- confusion["Pathogenic", "Benign"] / sum(confusion[, "Benign"])
# Sensitivity (Capture Rate): Pred Path / Actual Path
sensitivity <- confusion["Pathogenic", "Pathogenic"] / sum(confusion[, "Pathogenic"])

print(paste("Over-prediction Rate (FPR) on Stable Variants:", round(fpr * 100, 1), "%"))
print(paste("Capture Rate (Sensitivity) on Stable Variants:", round(sensitivity * 100, 1), "%"))
```
